observations:
Torah #256 is one of the shortest teachings in Likutay Moharan — a single sentence followed by a biblical proof-text. A new package requires three or more concepts connected by explicit bechina language forming an independent domain. This Torah contains no bechina language whatsoever.

The full text reads:
שֵׁם אַתָּה מְסֻגָּל עַל הַיָּם לְהַכְנִיעַ הַגַּלִּים, וְהַסּוֹד – בְּשׂוֹא גַלָּיו אַתָּה תְשַׁבְּחֵם (תהלים פט).

"The Name — you are effective over the sea to subdue the waves, and the secret is 'when its waves rise, You still them' (Psalms 89)."

Conceptual structure:
- שֵׁם (Name of God) → מְסֻגָּל עַל הַיָּם (power over the sea) → הַכְנָעַת הַגַּלִּים (subduing of the waves)

This is a pure eitza chain: the Name is the instrument; the sea/waves are the domain over which it acts; subduing is the result. The Rebbe does not declare that 'שֵׁם הוא בחינת גַּלִּים' or that 'יָּם נקרא שֵׁם' or any equivalent bechina equation. He states that the Name has power (מְסֻגָּל) over the sea — 'מְסֻגָּל' is an eitza attribution (fit for, effective for, has a special virtue for), not a bechina equation.

One might speculatively ask whether שֵׁם and הַכְנָעָה form a bechina pair (since the Name's essence is its power to humble), or whether יָּם and גַּלִּים are a bechina pair (the sea and its waves as two aspects of the same entity). However:
1. The text uses no bechina language to connect them.
2. Even יָּם and גַּלִּים — while closely related — are presented here as a unified object of action (what is subdued), not as two named aspects equated to each other through בְּחִינַת language.
3. Three or more concepts with explicit bechina interconnection are required; this teaching has zero.

The correct representation of this Torah in the map is as a minimal eitza structure: [שֵׁם] →eitza→ [הַכְנָעַת הַיָּם / גַּלִּים]. No package can be proposed.
